key_insight: Code is reframed from being just an output of LLMs to an operational substrate — a unified 'agent harness' that encodes reasoning, action, environment modeling, and execution-based verification to make agentic behavior more reliable and composable.
problem_solved: Agentic systems are fragmented and brittle because reasoning, acting, and verification are handled ad hoc; the paper addresses the lack of a unified, executable substrate for building, testing, and iterating on agents.
method: Introduce the conceptual framework 'code as agent harness' that treats code artifacts (scripts, modules, simulators, tests) as first-class substrates for agent behavior and evaluation.
Specify design patterns and primitives (harness templates, execution loops, simulation wrappers, assertive tests) that structure LLM outputs into executable and verifiable agent workflows.
Illustrate the approach with examples/benchmarks showing how execution-driven verification and iterative code refinement improve robustness and inspectability.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical design pattern to build more robust, debuggable, and composable agentic systems by leveraging code as the execution and verification backbone, accelerating reliable deployment and engineering iteration.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: LLM → generate harness code → execute in environment → verifier/tests → feedback loop
Before/After comparison: ad-hoc agent pipelines vs. harnessed-code agents (reliability, interpretability, modularity)
Component diagram of harness primitives: reasoner, executor, environment model, verifier
Small code snippet + execution trace showing iterative refinement from failing test to verified behavior
paper_authors: Xuying Ning, Katherine Tieu, Dongqi Fu, Tianxin Wei, Zihao Li
